tests.reason: The UNRESOLVED status is justified. The only supplied date, 01.01.1979, is expressly the commencement of the respondent's tenancy and is not tied to the alleged later subletting, assignment, or parting-with-possession transaction. Using that date for C01 would violate the supplied same-disposition binding requirement.

The proposed UNSUPPORTED status converts missing proof and sources undermining particular identity theories into affirmative refutation of the complete subletting proposition. The supplied material does not establish all required tenancy incidents for one identified subtenancy, but it also does not affirmatively establish that no qualifying subtenancy existed. The lower-court finding that particulars were lacking remains a prior-court finding and cannot be treated as target-court approval. The literal status is therefore UNRESOLVED. Local source review accepts UNRESOLVED because these are missing or contested factual predicates. The web reviewer incorrectly describes UNSUPPORTED as affirmative refutation; that characterization is rejected. UNSUPPORTED was never encoded as a negative class.

The proposed UNSUPPORTED status is stronger than the supplied material permits. No assignment transaction or assignee is identified, and no source establishes complete divestment of the respondent's tenancy rights. The respondent's statement that he continues in possession is contrary evidence, but it is a party statement and is not shown to be a target-court finding resolving the same alleged assignment. The result is inability to establish or refute C03, so the status is UNRESOLVED. Local source review accepts UNRESOLVED because these are missing or contested factual predicates. The web reviewer incorrectly describes UNSUPPORTED as affirmative refutation; that characterization is rejected. UNSUPPORTED was never encoded as a negative class.

The proposed UNSUPPORTED status rests principally on absence of affirmative proof of vesting and divestment. The respondent's continuing-possession statement is contrary evidence, but the supplied material does not establish that it resolves the same alleged arrangement and same relevant part of the premises at the target appellate stage. The lower-court finding about deficient particulars is likewise not target-court approval. C04 is therefore UNRESOLVED. Local source review accepts UNRESOLVED because these are missing or contested factual predicates. The web reviewer incorrectly describes UNSUPPORTED as affirmative refutation; that characterization is rejected. UNSUPPORTED was never encoded as a negative class.

The proposed UNSUPPORTED status improperly converts silence concerning written consent into affirmative proof that the statutory no-written-consent proposition is false. The supplied case material says nothing establishing either presence or absence of written consent for the same disposition, and the supplied law expressly contains no burden allocation permitting an inference from that silence. C05 is therefore UNRESOLVED. Local source review accepts UNRESOLVED because these are missing or contested factual predicates. The web reviewer incorrectly describes UNSUPPORTED as affirmative refutation; that characterization is rejected. UNSUPPORTED was never encoded as a negative class.
